facts.content: Patient has a dry, itchy rash on arms and hands for a few days.
facts.source_text: CC: Dry, itchy rash on arms/hands x few days

facts.content: The rash is erythematous, pruritic, and dry, began after swimming.
facts.source_text: HPI: Erythematous, pruritic, dry; began after swimming

facts.content: The rash has not spread to chest, legs, or face.
No fever or sweats noted.
No spots associated with the rash.
Coconut butter was applied without relief.
Patient feels tired.
Appetite, oral intake, bowels, and urination are normal.
No vomiting or diarrhea.
No prior history of skin diseases such as eczema or dermatitis.
Patient is taking Microgynon, a combined oral contraceptive pill.
Patient self-reports possible lactose intolerance.
Father has asthma and mother has hayfever.
No known family history of skin diseases.
facts.source_text: FH: no known family skin dz

facts.content: Patient is a primary school teacher experiencing increased work stress and long hours.
facts.source_text: SH: Primary school teacher; ↑work stress/long hours

facts.content: Patient lives alone.
Patient is a non-smoker, does not drink alcohol, and does not use recreational drugs.
facts.source_text: SH: non-smoker; no etOH; no recreational drugs

facts.content: Pruritic erythematous dry rash of hands/arms likely dermatitis.
facts.source_text: Assessment: Pruritic erythematous dry rash of hands/arms x few days, onset post-swimming; afebrile; no systemic sx — likely dermatitis

facts.content: There is work-related stress with associated fatigue.
Provide dermatitis patient information leaflet.
facts.source_text: Plan: Provide dermatitis patient information leaflet

facts.content: Start topical steroid cream on affected areas.
facts.source_text: Plan: Start topical steroid cream to affected areas (potency not specified)

facts.content: Use emollients liberally throughout the day.
facts.source_text: Plan: Emollients liberally throughout the day

facts.content: Over-the-counter antihistamines for itch: chlorphenamine (Piriton) or loratadine.
facts.source_text: Plan: OTC antihistamines for itch: chlorphenamine (Piriton) or loratadine

facts.content: Analgesics are not indicated.
Follow up next week if not improving; return earlier if worsening.
